# Velvet UI

> Velvet UI is the @velvetui/react package: headless, native-feeling React sheets and toasts with resilient gestures, nested stacks, and spring motion.

Install with `npm install @velvetui/react` or `bun add @velvetui/react`. Start with the sheet or toast quick start, then use the focused package subpaths and CSS entries for the pieces your interface needs.

## Start here

- [NPM package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@velvetui/react)
- [Current documentation](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0)
- [Interactive recipes](https://velvetui.co/recipes)
- [Interactive sheet gallery](https://velvetui.co/)
- [Interactive toast gallery](https://velvetui.co/toasts)
- [Agent invariant card](https://velvetui.co/INVARIANTS.md)
- [License options and terms](https://velvetui.co/?license=open)

## Documentation versions

- [0.3.0 (current)](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0)

## License summary

- Free: non-commercial use, unlimited projects, forever access, and free support.
- Individual: $20 plus tax for commercial use by an individual or a team with fewer than three members.
- Organization: $129 plus tax for commercial use limited to one organization.
- Codebase access: contact sales through the license dialog.

## Documentation 0.3.0

- [Overview](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0): Velvet UI is a headless React sheet and toast toolkit built around composable primitives, resilient gestures, and WAAPI-driven motion. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/overview.md))
- [Installation](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/installation): Install Velvet UI, then import the structural stylesheet required by the primitive or composition you use. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/installation.md))
- [Package exports](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/package-exports): Choose focused JavaScript and CSS entry points for smaller bundles, predictable style order, and server-rendered React applications. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/package-exports.md))
- [Server rendering](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/server-rendering): Keep routes server rendered while placing the smallest possible client boundary around interactive sheets, portals, and toast calls. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/server-rendering.md))
- [Styling](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/styling): Velvet exposes semantic classes and CSS custom properties so the component can inherit your design system without a styling runtime. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/styling.md))
- [Bring your own components](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/custom-components): Keep Velvet's gestures, focus, accessibility, and motion while your design system owns every visible element. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/custom-components.md))
- [CSS reference](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/css-reference): Use the stable CSS entries, variables, and semantic data hooks without depending on internal wrapper order. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/css-reference.md))
- [Sheet quick start](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/sheet-quick-start): A Sheet groups a trigger, portal, motion surface, accessible title, description, and close action under one controlled or uncontrolled state. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/sheet-quick-start.md))
- [Anatomy](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/anatomy): The primitive tree separates state, trigger, portal, view, backdrop, content, and accessible labels. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/anatomy.md))
- [Nested modal navigation](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/nested-modal-navigation): Keep a side sheet inside a centered modal with an independent native scrollbar, swipe-back through content, and separate Back and Close actions. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/nested-modal-navigation.md))
- [Gallery recipes](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/gallery-recipes): The gallery demonstrates production-shaped layouts such as bottom sheets, drawers, modals, detents, lightboxes, and persistent surfaces. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/gallery-recipes.md))
- [Open state](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/open-state): Sheets support uncontrolled defaults and controlled state for coordination with your router, form flow, or application state. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/open-state.md))
- [Placement](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/placement): The panel side determines both the origin and the dismiss direction: bottom, top, left, right, or center. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/placement.md))
- [Detents](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/detents): Snap points create intermediate resting positions without a separate gesture implementation. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/detents.md))
- [Dismissal](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/dismissal): Dismissal is configurable per view: gestures, outside press, and Escape can each be allowed, prevented, or decided at runtime. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/dismissal.md))
- [Travel animation](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/travel-animation): Travel animation maps a shared open progress value onto any visual property, keeping panel, backdrop, and surrounding UI synchronized. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/travel-animation.md))
- [Shared-origin motion](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/shared-origin-motion): SheetMorph starts content at the trigger or a supplied element’s measured geometry, then settles it into its authored layout. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/shared-origin-motion.md))
- [Springs](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/springs): Presets make interaction tuning consistent across a product while retaining an escape hatch for custom physical values. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/springs.md))
- [Motion API](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/motion-api): Use Velvet's interruptible springs, WAAPI orchestration, travel interpolation, reduced-motion handling, and React lifecycle hooks anywhere. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/motion-api.md))
- [Triggers and actions](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/triggers): Trigger, Close, and Step communicate intent directly and can render through your own button using asChild. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/triggers.md))
- [Accessibility](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/accessibility): Modal sheets apply dialog semantics, focus management, Escape handling, inert background treatment, and focus restoration. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/accessibility.md))
- [Sheet API](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/sheet-api): The sheet API is assembled from state, view, content, and action primitives so consumers can adopt only the layers they need. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/sheet-api.md))
- [Depth Sheet](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/depth-sheet): DepthSheet gives a full-width surface the visual hierarchy of iOS stacked sheets by scaling and rounding the page behind it. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/depth-sheet.md))
- [Card Expansion](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/card-expansion): CardExpansion opens a card into a focused modal surface while retaining the scale and edge response expected from a lightbox. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/card-expansion.md))
- [Styled compositions](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/styled-compositions): Styled compositions package the visual grammar for common interactions while preserving the underlying primitive API. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/styled-compositions.md))
- [Composition API](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/composition-api): Compare every supplied composition, its parts, defaults, escape hatches, and CSS contract. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/composition-api.md))
- [Toast quick start](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-quick-start): Render one Toaster near the application root and call toast from any client interaction. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-quick-start.md))
- [Toast variants](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-variants): Toast variants cover neutral, success, error, warning, info, loading, action, promise, and custom JSX states. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-variants.md))
- [Toast positioning](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-positioning): The Toaster supports the six viewport corners and centers with a fixed viewport layer that does not inherit local layout offsets. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-positioning.md))
- [Toast options](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-options): Toast options control duration, description, action, close affordance, visual treatment, and stacked expansion. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-options.md))
- [Toast promise](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-promise): toast.promise binds an async result to one continuous feedback item with loading, success, and error states. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-promise.md))
- [Toast API](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-api): The toast API is a small imperative dispatcher with a single declarative renderer, Toaster. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/toast-api.md))
- [Scroll coordination](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/scroll): A scrollable sheet hands a drag to the sheet only when its internal Scroll.View reaches the matching boundary. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/scroll.md))
- [Scroll API](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/scroll-api): Coordinate nested scrolling, virtual keyboards, focus, progress, and imperative spring scrolling. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/scroll-api.md))
- [Sheet stacks](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/sheet-stack): SheetStack coordinates layering, backdrop ownership, focus restoration, and depth transforms for any number of nested sheets. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/sheet-stack.md))
- [Utilities](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/utilities): Utilities cover scroll coordination, visually hidden labels, autofocus targets, fixed surfaces, islands, and external overlays. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/utilities.md))
- [Troubleshooting](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/troubleshooting): Diagnose missing styles, swallowed refs, controlled-state loops, gesture handoff, mobile keyboards, nested sheets, and third-party portals. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/troubleshooting.md))
- [Production checklist](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/production-checklist): A manual release checklist for state, gestures, scroll, mobile keyboards, accessibility, arbitrary-depth stacks, portals, and bundle cost. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/production-checklist.md))
- [Documentation versions](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/versions): Use an explicit documentation version when implementing or maintaining an application on a known Velvet UI release. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/versions.md))
- [Changelog](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/changelog): Release notes for changes that affect installation, APIs, styling, behavior, performance, or upgrades. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/docs/0.3.0/changelog.md))

## Runnable recipes

- [Route-controlled sheet](https://velvetui.co/recipes/route-controlled-sheet): Open from URL state, cold-open without a trigger, and update navigation only after exit motion completes. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/route-controlled-sheet.md))
- [Async editor close](https://velvetui.co/recipes/async-editor-close): Flush a dirty draft at the dismissal-request boundary before committing controlled state or starting exit motion. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/async-editor-close.md))
- [Destructive confirmation](https://velvetui.co/recipes/destructive-confirmation): Give destructive work an alert-dialog role, a safe initial target, and dismissal ownership while the mutation is busy. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/destructive-confirmation.md))
- [Nested modal navigation](https://velvetui.co/recipes/nested-modal-navigation): A centered library with a body-safe native scroller and a right-side detail surface that swipes back independently. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/nested-modal-navigation.md))
- [Nested navigation with Tailwind v4](https://velvetui.co/recipes/nested-modal-navigation-tailwind-v4): The same nested modal architecture expressed with Tailwind v4 while preserving structural CSS and gesture handoff. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/nested-modal-navigation-tailwind-v4.md))
- [Detail → confirmation → lightbox](https://velvetui.co/recipes/nested-detail-confirmation-lightbox): Compose host-relative navigation, an alert dialog, and a family-correct Lightbox without losing dismissal order. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/nested-detail-confirmation-lightbox.md))
- [Radix popover in a Sheet](https://velvetui.co/recipes/radix-popover-in-sheet): Keep Radix positioning and focus behavior while enrolling its portaled Content in Velvet dismissal ownership. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/radix-popover-in-sheet.md))
- [React Aria popover in a Sheet](https://velvetui.co/recipes/react-aria-popover-in-sheet): Let React Aria own accessible popover semantics while Velvet coordinates the parent modal and dismissal stack. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/react-aria-popover-in-sheet.md))
- [Base UI popover in a Sheet](https://velvetui.co/recipes/base-ui-popover-in-sheet): Place Velvet's Base UI boundary inside Popover.Portal and slot the real Positioner, leaving Base UI in charge of layout. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/base-ui-popover-in-sheet.md))
- [Reduced-motion initial-open sheet](https://velvetui.co/recipes/reduced-motion-initial-open): Prove that a controlled draggable sheet mounted open never turns setup-time runway normalization into a false close. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/reduced-motion-initial-open.md))
- [Deleted-trigger focus fallback](https://velvetui.co/recipes/deleted-trigger-focus-fallback): Restore focus safely when the control that opened a sheet disappears during an optimistic update. ([Markdown](https://velvetui.co/recipes/deleted-trigger-focus-fallback.md))
